To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LCN2 controls the expression and the number of cells expressing SDF-1, the chemokine involved in the recruitment of hematopoietic precursors to the bone marrow.
LCN2 controls the expression and the number of CD133+CXCR4+ progenitor cells in bone.
LCN2 is expressed in osteoblasts and that LCN2 controls the number of CD-34+ cells in bone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the role of Lcn2 in the regulation of the number of CD 34+/CXCR 4+ cells in the bone and bone marrow microenvironment.
the role of Lcn2 in the bone/blood system.
the identification of novel molecules that could contribute to the regulation of the bone marrow stem cells and their niches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LCN2 is a factor that can be used to control the expression of Sdf-1 and the proliferation rate of CD34+/CXC4+ cells in the bone/bm microenvironment.
LCN2 controls the expression and the number of SDF- 1 responsive cells in bone.
LCN2 controls the expression and the number of cells expressing SDF-1 in the bone marrow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LCN2 controls the expression level of SDF- 1 and the number (proliferation?) of responsive cells in the bone.
LCN2 is able to control the expression of Sdf-1 and the proliferation of CD34+/CXR4+ cells.
the LCN2 is a new regulator of SDF-2 expression in bone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LCN2 is a key regulator of the bone marrow stem cell niche and that this effect could be mediated by its role on the expression of SFD-1.
the expression of LCN2 in bone could be a new factor contributing to the maintenance of the bone marrow niche.
LCN2 can be considered a new factor controlling the number of precursor cells in the hematopoietic niche and thus the bone marrow micro-environment.
